summary: Bug hunt under his standing brief (#690): six areas, real touch/mouse input, every finding a failing test; one skeptic per finding; a fixer per area

confirmed.title: A new project's picked aspect and resolution are thrown away by the first clip or photo he adds
confirmed.see: He opens New project and picks 16:9 Wide at 1080p, so the dialog says 1920 x 1080. He taps Create and adds his portrait phone clip first. The project silently becomes 1080 x 1920 portrait. The canvas he chose is gone, the preview turns portrait, and the export comes out portrait. The same thing happens with every tile: a 9:16 1080p pick becomes 2160 x 3840 as soon as his first clip is 4K, and an iPhone photo turns it into 2160 x 2880. Only the Custom tile is labelled Auto adjusts (his wording, #659), but all five of the other tiles adjust too.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a a new project keeps the aspect and size he picked when the first thing he adds is a phone clip of another shape. It fails at 380 and at desktop width with: he picked 16:9 Wide at 1080p in New project (1920 x 1080) and added his portrait phone clip first — the project silently became 1080 x 1920: the canvas he chose is gone, the preview turned portrait and the export will come out 1080 x 1920. Only the Custom tile says Auto adjusts. The dialog is driven with a real finger at 360 (+, 16:9, Create), and the clip comes in through #file-input's change event. A throwaway patch that skips the resize turns it green.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:2783-2785 in FM.addMediaLayer does `if (first && rec.width && rec.height) { const fit = FM.fitProjectSize(rec.width, rec.height); P.width = fit.w; P.height = fit.h; ...}` for any empty project. Nothing records how the project was sized. js/home.js:2684 createFromDialog passes the chosen width and height to FM.projects.create, and js/storage.js create() stores them with no flag, so the dialog's choice can't be told apart from a default. index.html:725 labels only the Custom tile Auto adjusts.
confirmed.fix: Resize on the first import only when the project was made with Custom (Auto adjusts) or with no explicit choice. Stamp that on the project in createFromDialog and read it in addMediaLayer. A clip whose shape doesn't match the canvas is then fit-scaled into it, like any later clip.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it: the test fails at desktop width and at --width 380 on port 8921, with the same message the hunter reported. The fixture is fair. The dialog is driven by real touches (+, 16:9 Wide, Create). Before the import, the test checks that the new project really is 1920x1080 and empty. The clip then arrives through #file-input's change event, which is the same handler the Add sheet and the timeline's Import media use (js/addmenu.js:42, js/app.js:6254 → FM.addMediaLayer at js/app.js:4937-4938). The media library route (js/medialib.js:252) goes through the same function.

The code path is plain. js/app.js FM.addMediaLayer runs `if (first && rec.width && rec.height) { const fit = FM.fitProjectSize(rec.width, rec.height); P.width = fit.w; P.height = fit.h; ... resizeCanvas(); }` for any empty project. Nothing records how the project was sized, and it only shows a toast when the size was capped. So when the aspect or resolution changes this way, he is not told.

Nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for this. It is the reverse of what he asked for. The first-import resize comes from before the full New project dialog (v3.68, his request "show all of the edit options you could ever hope for"), and the two were never reconciled. The v9.27 log that capped the resize described it as "the size the app picks unasked", and a tile picked in the dialog is not unasked. #659, in his words, labels only the Custom tile "Auto adjusts" (index.html:725). That implies the other five tiles hold, yet the Custom tile has no auto-adjust behaviour of its own: all six tiles behave the same (js/home.js createFromDialog → FM.projects.create with no flag). The app is also modelled on Alight Motion, where the ratio you pick stays and a clip is fitted inside it.

He would hit this in normal use. His default is 9:16 at 1080p, and adding a stock iPhone photo first turns that into 2160x2880, which is 3:4. The existing proj-cap test confirms fitProjectSize(3024,4032) gives exactly that. A 4K clip turns a 1080p pick into 2160x3840, the kind of oversized project he has already measured as laggy (#202). Picking 16:9 and then adding a portrait clip flips the canvas, the preview and the export to portrait.

This is not a synthetic-event artefact, a timing assumption or a state he can't reach. I edited nothing.

confirmed.title: Replace media keeps the old pixel scale, so the new clip or photo comes in at the wrong size (2x for a 4K swap)
confirmed.see: He uses the ⋯ menu's Replace media… to swap his 1080 x 1920 clip for his 4K portrait clip, which has the same shape. The new clip comes in at twice the width and height: 2160 px wide on a 1080 px canvas. He sees only the middle quarter of it, and its edges are cut off. A 12 MP photo swapped in for a 1080p clip comes in about 2.8x too big, and a small file swapped in comes in tiny. Filling a template slot through Insert your Media and its Replace Media button goes the same way, since that button calls the same function.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Replace media puts the new clip where the old one was at the same size, instead of blowing it up by its pixel count. It fails with: he swapped his 1080 x 1920 clip for a 4K portrait clip of the same shape with Replace media — the new clip came in 2.00 times the size, 2160 px wide on the 1080 px canvas, so only its middle quarter shows: the left edge of the canvas is blue where the clip green border should be. Filling a template slot (Insert your Media) with his own 4K clip or 12 MP photo goes the same way. The ⋯ and Replace media… are tapped with a real finger at 360, and only the file picker's own sheet is stood in for. A throwaway patch that rescales by old.width/new.width turns it green.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:4258-4276 FM.replaceMediaWith swaps the record (`FM.media.set(id, nrec); layer.type = nrec.kind;` at 4265-4266) and re-clamps only the timing. transform.scale is never touched. js/compositor.js:15927 FM.layerSize returns `{ w: m.width, h: m.height }`, so the drawn size is the file's pixel size times the old scale. js/template-fill.js:249 goes through the same FM.replaceMedia.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I ran the test in the hunt3-a worktree on port 8921 and it fails exactly as reported: after the swap the 4K clip draws 2160 px wide on the 1080 px canvas, 2.00 times too big, and the left edge of the canvas shows the clip's blue middle instead of its green border.

How the code causes it:
- On import, js/app.js:2805-2806 sets transform.scale to fit the file into the canvas: min(P.width/rec.width, P.height/rec.height). So a 1080p clip gets scale 1 and a 4K clip gets 0.5.
- FM.replaceMediaWith (js/app.js:4258-4276) swaps the media record and sets layer.type, and changes only trimStart and duration. It never touches transform.scale.
- FM.layerSize (js/compositor.js:15911-15912) returns the file's own pixel size.
- The loaders keep the native size, with no proxy or cap: js/media.js:168 uses videoWidth/videoHeight, and js/media.js:618 uses naturalWidth/naturalHeight.
- So the drawn size is the new file's pixels times the scale that suited the old file. A 4K clip coming in for a 1080p one comes in twice as big, and a 12 MP photo (4032 px) about 3.7 times as big.

Template slots have the same bug. The Replace Media button in js/template-fill.js:249 calls the same FM.replaceMedia, and REQUESTS.md (#~9404, v9.97) only records that the swap "keeps the transform". That describes the code. It is not something he asked for, and nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for the new file to keep the old pixel scale.

The test is not an artefact:
- The fixture is a real H.264 MP4 encoded in the page.
- The first clip goes through the app's own #file-input change handler.
- The ⋯ menu and Replace media… are tapped with real touch input at 360 px wide.
- The only stand-in is the file picker sheet (HTMLInputElement.click is replaced to hand over the file), which a real picker would do the same way.
- The pixel check renders through FM.renderScene, the same path the preview and export use.
- The worktree's replaceMediaWith is identical to main's.

He would hit this on almost every swap from his phone, because it shoots 4K clips and 12 MP stills.

confirmed.title: An animated GIF imports as a still: frame 0 in the preview and in every export
confirmed.see: He adds a reaction GIF or an animated sticker from the Add sheet, or drops one on the PC. The app takes it (.gif is on its image list), puts it on the timeline and shows it on the canvas, but it never moves. In the test the canvas shows the first frame (red) at 0.1, 0.35, 0.6 and 0.85 s of a four-colour, one-second GIF. I checked the exporter: it renders every frame as that same first frame. Nothing tells him the animation was dropped.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a an animated GIF he adds moves on the canvas, instead of freezing on its first frame. It fails with: his animated GIF (four frames a second, red, blue, green, yellow) is frozen on its first frame — the canvas shows red at 0.1 s, red at 0.35 s, red at 0.6 s, red at 0.85 s. It never moves, in the preview or in the export. A control uses ImageDecoder to confirm the browser reads the fixture as 4 frames with frame 3 green, and the GIF is imported through #file-input's change event.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:4863 RE_IMAGE includes gif, and handleFiles sends it to FM.loadImageFile. js/media.js:614-622 FM.loadImageFile loads it into a detached `new Image()` that is never in the document, so its animation never advances. js/compositor.js:14797 draws `src = m.el`, which is always frame 0. The exporter renders through the same FM.renderScene (js/exporter.js:1330/1572/1641). I checked in a probe that the export frames at 0.0 to 0.9 s all read 230,30,30. There is no ImageDecoder or other GIF frame handling anywhere in js/.
confirmed.fix: For image/gif (and animated webp/apng), decode the frames with ImageDecoder where it exists and keep them with their durations on the record. The compositor then picks the frame from the layer's local time, looping, the way it already picks from a frameCache. Where ImageDecoder is missing, a toast saying the GIF will import as a still is better than silence.

verdict.reason:
This is a real defect. I ran the test in the hunt3-a worktree on port 8921 and it failed exactly as reported: the canvas centre is red at 0.1, 0.35, 0.6 and 0.85 s. Its control passes, so the fixture really is a four-frame, four-colour GIF (ImageDecoder reads 4 frames and frame 3 is green).

The code path matches the report:
- **He can reach it.** `#file-input` accepts `image/*` (index.html:658), `RE_IMAGE` includes `gif` (js/app.js:4863), and the file goes to `FM.loadImageFile` (js/media.js:614-622). That puts it in a plain `new Image()` that is never added to the page.
- **Nothing reads the frames.** `grep` finds no `ImageDecoder` and no GIF frame handling anywhere in js/. The only GIF code is the export encoder.
- **Nothing warns him.** The import path has no toast or message saying the animation was dropped.

I also checked it in a browser, outside the timeline. I loaded the same GIF with `FM.loadImageFile` and drew it with `drawImage` every 200 ms for 1 s, once detached and once attached to the page. Every draw was 230,30,30, the first frame. That fits the HTML spec: `drawImage` of an animated image uses its default or first frame. So this is not a test timing artefact: synchronous `renderScene` calls did not cause it, and waiting in real time changes nothing.

The preview and the exporter both render through `FM.renderScene`, and a timeline render at time t cannot pick a frame from a wall-clock animation anyway. So the GIF is frozen in the export too.

REQUESTS.md has no request or Held note about importing GIFs as stills. The GIF entries there are about GIF export (#669 and the v16.95 speed fix). This is not behaviour he asked for.

The result is a reaction GIF or animated sticker that imports without complaint and never moves. Medium severity is fair.

I edited nothing. The browser check only created and removed a temporary image on the worktree's own localhost page, and no project was made. The dev server on port 8921 is still running in the background.

confirmed.title: Replace media on a song can't take a song: the picker offers only video and photos, and a song given to it is refused
confirmed.see: He selects his song, taps ⋯ and gets Replace media… (a song is a picture-less video layer, and a template's Insert your Media also lists it as a slot). The picker opens for video/*,image/* only, so on his iPhone every song in Files is greyed out. If a song reaches it anyway, on PC with All files, it is loaded as a photo, fails, and the toast says Could not load that file. The layer keeps the old song. The only way to try a different track is to delete the layer and lose its cuts, volume and fades.
confirmed.test: HUNT-a Replace media on a song lets him pick another song, and the layer then plays it. It fails with: Replace media… on his song opens a picker for video/*,image/* only — on his iPhone every song in Files is greyed out, and Song B handed to it anyway was refused (toast: Could not load that file) — the layer still plays Song A.wav. The ⋯ and Replace media… are tapped with a real finger at 360. A throwaway patch that adds audio to accept and to isVideo turns it green, and the clip's 6 s cut is kept.
confirmed.evidence: js/app.js:4692-4693 offers Replace media… for any `layer.type === 'video'`, which includes songs. js/app.js:4283 in FM.replaceMedia sets `input.accept = 'video/*,image/*'`. js/app.js:4287 `const isVideo = /^video\//.test(file.type) || /\.(mp4|mov|webm|mkv|m4v)$/i.test(file.name);` sends an audio/* file to FM.loadImageFile, which rejects, so replaceMedia toasts 'Could not load that file' and returns.
confirmed.fix: When the layer is a song (a video record with no width or height), open the picker with the Add ▸ Audio accept list (FM._audioAccept). In FM.replaceMedia, use FM.mediaKind(file) and load audio through FM.loadVideoFile, like handleFiles does, so the song replaces the song and the layer keeps its cuts and volume.

verdict.reason: I ran the test in the worktree and it failed the way the report says: the picker asks for 'video/*,image/*', the song is refused with the toast 'Could not load that file', and the layer still plays Song A.wav. The code agrees. A song is not its own layer type: handleFiles in js/app.js loads an audio file through FM.loadVideoFile as a video layer with no picture. So the layer ⋯ menu (js/app.js:4692-4693, `layer.type === 'video' || 'image'`) offers 'Replace media…' for his song, and template-fill.js kindOf() also lists it as a 'media' slot. FM.replaceMedia (js/app.js:4279-4290) hard-codes `input.accept = 'video/*,image/*'`, so on iOS every song in Files is greyed out. It then decides video-or-image with its own regex, which ignores audio, so an audio/* file goes to FM.loadImageFile, which fails, and the toast fires. The test itself is fair. The song goes in through the app's own #file-input change handler, the same way Add does it. ⋯ and Replace media… are tapped with real touch input at 360px. The picker stub only stands in for the OS dialog and records what the app asked for; it cannot cause the refusal, because the refusal comes from the app's own type check. REQUESTS.md has nothing saying a song should be kept out of Replace media, and the menu offers it anyway, so a button that always fails on a song is a real defect. His only way round it is to delete the layer and re-add, which loses its cuts, volume and fades. Medium severity is right: nothing is lost, but a menu item he can reach does not work.

A touch that lands on the line is therefore implicitly captured by the notch. js/inspector.js tickStrip's pointermove calls `strip.setPointerCapture(pend.id)` after the 6px lock, which moves capture from the notch to the strip. The browser then fires lostpointercapture at the notch, and that event bubbles to js/inspector.js:1027 `strip.addEventListener('lostpointercapture', end)`, which ends the drag after the first applied notch. The recorded event log was: pointermove(+1 notch) → lostpointercapture → gotpointercapture → pointermoves with no change. The visual Blur slider reproduced it identically. verdict.reason:
I re-ran the test on port 8922 and it fails the same way the hunter said. A real CDP touch drag of 80 px that starts 40 px beside the centre line takes Volume from 100 to 155%. The same drag started on the centre line gives 105%, which is one notch.

The code path explains it:
- styles.css:1727 `.fx-scrub-notch` has no `pointer-events: none`, unlike `.fx-scrub-ticks` at 1721. A touch on the 2 px cyan line therefore hits the notch element.
- On a touch, the browser automatically captures the pointer to whatever element the finger landed on. Chrome does this, and WebKit/iOS does too (PointerCaptureController sets it on pointerdown for touch).
- tickStrip in js/inspector.js does not claim the touch on pointerdown. After 6 px of travel it calls `strip.setPointerCapture(pend.id)`, which moves the capture from the notch to the strip.
- The browser then fires `lostpointercapture` at the notch. That event bubbles, so it reaches `strip.addEventListener('lostpointercapture', end)` at js/inspector.js:1027. `end()` sets drag to null and commits.
- The move that triggered the lock has already applied one notch. Every later move returns at `if (!drag) return`.

When the touch starts off the line, it lands on the strip itself (the ticks and marks ignore touches). The strip already holds the capture, so setting it again changes nothing, no `lostpointercapture` fires, and the drag completes. That is why the control passes, and it isolates the cause: the two drags differ only in where they start.

This is not a test artefact:
- The input is real touch through the browser's pointer pipeline, not synthetic events.
- The timing is an ordinary drag at 10 px per 30 ms.
- A finger can plausibly land on the line, and it is the bright mark people tend to aim for.
- It is not intended behaviour. REQUESTS.md has no related complaint or request.

The mouse path is not affected, because it captures to the strip on pointerdown, before any touch-style capture exists. So this bug is phone-only, which is his main device.

Every tickStrip ruler is affected: Volume, the fades and all the effect sliders. Severity is modest: it only happens when the touch starts inside the 2 px line, and he can lift and grab again. But when it happens he sees it, as a slider that moves one step and then stops following his finger.

The proposed fix is correct: add `pointer-events: none` on the notch, and ignore a bubbled `lostpointercapture` by checking `e.target === strip`. I edited nothing and stopped the server afterwards.

The pointerdown handler just above it records only the position, for the hold-to-pin gesture. By contrast js/app.js:7935 fires the M key on keydown, the moment of the press. The test made three real 110ms taps on #tl-headtap during playback and read FM.time with a capture listener at each real pointerdown. CONTROL: all three presses made a mark and playback kept running.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced it. On the hunt3-b worktree (server on 8922, which is serving that tree) the test fails with the marks 4.5, 4.5 and 4.5 frames after the finger touched. The control held: 3 real presses, 3 bookmarks, and playback still running.

The bookmark itself is dropped from the 'click' listener (line 6169). That calls FM.toggleMarkerAtPlayhead (line 1462), which stamps `const t = FM.time` at that moment, and a click fires on release. So during playback every mark is late by however long the finger stayed down. The M key (line 7935) runs on keydown, so the same beat lands in different places on PC and phone. The app has no latency compensation anywhere: no outputLatency or baseLatency, and no beat snapping.

This is not a test artefact. The test uses trusted CDP touches through the browser's real touch-to-pointer-to-click pipeline, a person can reach this state (tap the bookmark while the song plays), and nothing in REQUESTS.md asks for release-time stamping. Queue 364 only asked for 'tap the top of the playhead to add bookmarks'. The hold gesture needs the release to tell a tap from a hold, but not to decide the time. The thumbnail hold pauses playback anyway, so stamping the press time while playing does not conflict with it.

The test holds each tap for 110 ms, and the extra frame or so is harness dispatch plus rAF granularity. That is still above 1 frame for any real tap, and audio arriving about 100 ms before a visual cut is noticeable. REQUESTS.md has no record of Ezra marking beats live, but the app is modelled on Alight Motion, where play-and-tap-bookmark is the usual way to mark beats. Speaker or Bluetooth latency already makes his marks late, and stamping at release adds to that.

confirmed.see: He pinches a group smaller (or turns it). During playback, a layer in that group that has no animation jumps about 100 px the moment another layer in the same group comes on screen. While another member slides in, the still layers drift about 100 px across the canvas with it. It happens in the preview and in the exported video. confirmed.evidence: js/compositor.js:2412-2419 applyParentChain calls FM.groupPivot(pl, scene, t) on every frame whenever the group's rotation or scale is not zero or one. FM.groupPivot (js/compositor.js:15981) takes groupBoundsLocal (js/compositor.js:15938-15961), which drops any member not on screen at t ('if (!FM.isLayerVisibleAt(l, t)) return;') and reads each member's x/y at t. So the pivot follows which members are visible and where they are at that moment. canvas-edit.js parentXform (line 176) and FM.groupBounds use the same moving pivot.
confirmed.fix: Give the group a stored pivot instead of one measured every frame. For example, write the members' box centre into the group's anchor (in child space) once, when the group is made or when he moves its anchor, and have applyParentChain, groupBounds, parentXform and bakeGroupTransform all read that stored point. When membership changes (add, delete or ungroup a member), re-bake the stored pivot so nothing moves at that moment.

verdict.reason:
This is a real bug. I ran the test myself at 1280 and at 380 and it fails the same way both times, with the numbers the hunter reported. In a group scaled to 70%, the red square has no animation, but it jumps 108 px (from 300,600 to 360,690) at 2 s. That is the moment the blue layer in the same group comes on screen. When blue slides across instead, red drifts 102 px. With the group turned 20 degrees instead of scaled, red drifts 120 px.

The code path matches the report. In js/compositor.js at lines 2414-2419, applyParentChain calls FM.groupPivot(pl, scene, t) on every frame whenever a group's rotation is not 0 or its scale is not 1. FM.groupPivot (line 15981) gets its box from FM.groupBoundsLocal (lines 15938-15961). That function skips any member that is not visible at time t (`if (!FM.isLayerVisibleAt(l, t)) return;`) and reads each member's x/y at t. pivotIn then takes the anchor as a fraction of that live box. So the point a scaled or rotated group turns around moves whenever a member appears, disappears or moves, and the still members get drawn somewhere else. The numbers check out by hand: at 1.5 s only red is on screen, so the pivot is red's centre and red stays at 300,600. At 2.5 s the pivot is the centre of both squares, (500,900), so red lands at 500+0.7*(300-500)=360 and 900+0.7*(600-900)=690.

The test setup is realistic, not an artefact:
- It writes g.transform.scale = 0.7 directly, and that is exactly what his pinch and the corner handle write. In js/canvas-edit.js (around lines 330, 433, 520 and 629), sandwich is true for any group with members, so the UI writes only scale or rotation and leaves the pivoting to the renderer.
- The group is made with the real FM.groupSelection.
- Positions are measured from ink drawn by FM.renderScene itself, which the test's own comments say is the same draw path the preview and the export use.
- The test checks an unscaled group first as a control, and that case correctly shows no movement, so the fixture is not what is moving the square.

Layers that start at different times inside one group (a title that appears after the background, say) are ordinary, and scaling or turning a group is exactly what #630 was built for him to do. The #630 entry in REQUESTS.md asked for groups to scale "about the middle". Nothing there asks for the middle to be re-measured live, and still layers jumping when a sibling appears is plainly not what he wanted, so this is not requested behaviour.

The same moving pivot is also read by FM.groupBounds (the selection box and hit-test), canvas-edit.js parentXform (line 177) and bakeGroupTransform, which measures at t=0 only. So the selection box also drifts, and ungrouping a scaled group whose members are not all visible at 0 s would bake them about a different pivot than the one they were drawn with.

verdict.reason: This is a real bug he would hit. I re-ran the test on port 8925 at 380px and it failed as reported: the slot chip is still the template teal [42,157,143]. In my run the big preview did show his photo, but only because the small test PNG decoded in time. The code confirms it. In js/template-fill.js:246-257 the Replace Media click calls FM.replaceMedia(id) without waiting for it. The only refreshes are a one-time window 'focus' listener and a 1.2 s timer, and each calls drawSlots() and then select(), which queues one paint. The swap itself is async inside FM.replaceMedia's change handler (js/app.js:4279+). It awaits FM.loadImageFile (image onload, js/media.js:614) and then FM.storage.stashPrevMedia (an IndexedDB write), and only then calls replaceMediaWith. verdict.reason:

I re-ran the test on the unfixed worktree (hunt3-e, clean tree at 8aa929f7) on port 8925 and it failed the same way: the words slot had 0 lit pixels and the strip slot had 0 orange ones. - FM.renderScene (js/compositor.js:15546-15550) works out its own scale from the canvas: 108 / 1080 = 0.1 for a phone-shaped project. baseT (js/compositor.js:14253) then calls setTransform, which throws away the chip's translate and scale.

- clearRect(0,0,P.width,P.height) at that scale covers the whole chip, which also wipes the #0a0f16 background drawThumb had just filled in.

I re-ran the test on the unfixed worktree (hunt3-e, clean tree at 8aa929f7) on port 8925 and it failed the same way: the words slot had 0 lit pixels and the strip slot had 0 orange ones. verdict.reason:

The tap in the test is a real one: tests/_cdp.py turns on touch emulation and sends a touchStart and touchEnd 60 ms apart, so it goes through Chrome's own tap handling, not a synthetic .click().

Why it happens:
- All three backdrops close as soon as the finger goes down: js/shortcuts.js:125 (the ? sheet), js/notepad.js:119 (Notes) and js/app.js:7668 (Canvas settings). The ? and Notes backdrops use display:none; Canvas settings is hidden the same way.

He can reach this. I checked a 375px phone view in the browser. With a layer selected, the phone top bar still shows ? next to the bin (styles.css:3844-3847 only hides the project buttons in editing mode). The ? card starts just below the bar at y=57. The dimmed layer (62% dark) sits over the bar, so the ? and the bin show through it, dimmed. The spot over the bin is the backdrop itself, not the card. So "tap the ? again to close" or "tap the top bar to get out" are both natural moves:
- Tapping ?, Notes or the cog again makes the panel flash shut and open again.

As I understand it, iOS WebKit decides where a tap's click goes only after the finger lifts, which is the well-known ghost-click problem. What is measured is Chrome's real touch handling.

It is not intended behaviour. Closing on an outside tap was asked for (#252), but pressing whatever is under the finger was not, and #762 asks for the opposite on the opener.
